thread.title: St. George plans Uber rideshare program, residents question use of city funds - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: St. George plans Uber rideshare program, residents question use of city funds - NewsBreak

author: Ethan Goode
title: St. George plans Uber rideshare program, residents question use of city funds - NewsBreak
text:
By Ethan Goode ,
2 hours ago
ST. GEORGE, La. (Louisiana First) — A new transportation option could soon be available to people traveling around St. George, but the city’s plan to subsidize Uber rides is also raising questions from some residents about how public dollars are being spent.
The City of St. George is preparing to launch a 12-month rideshare pilot program in partnership with Uber. The program is expected to begin in late 2026 and is designed to give residents another option for getting around the newly incorporated city.
Under the proposed program, 50% of the cost of an eligible Uber ride would be subsidized. Participants would be allowed up to 10 subsidized rides per month.
St. George Mayor Pro Tem Drew Murrill said the program is intended to provide transportation for trips within the city.
“Local trips within the boundaries of St. George after you originate and end in the city limits of St. George,” Murrill said.
Eligible trips must generally begin and end within St. George. However, the city plans to make exceptions for trips to and from four medical facilities: Our Lady of the Lake Regional Medical Center, Baton Rouge General Medical Center, Woman’s Hospital and Ochsner Health Center - O’Neal.
City officials say the pilot will also allow St. George to collect data on transportation demand and how residents use the service. That information could eventually help determine where the city should make future transportation investments.
The pilot is projected to serve approximately 1,500 to 2,000 riders, depending on enrollment and available funding.
Murrill said the program could reach residents who may not currently use traditional public transportation.
“This is public transportation. It’s supposed to be available to the entire public,” Murrill said. “And right now, there’s a sizable portion of our population that does not utilize public transportation.”
Some residents question spending While city leaders see the program as a way to expand transportation options, some residents are questioning whether subsidizing Uber rides should be a priority as St. George continues building its city government.
St. George resident Helen Mason said she wants more information about the city’s spending and whether future projects could ultimately affect taxpayers.
“With a new $25 million construction project, are we going to be in our budget or is this going to result in a new tax millage on our taxes, property taxes that we keep seeing increase year after year?” Mason said.
Mason also raised questions about the procedures used to allocate money toward city programs and said she would like to see those processes clearly documented.
She suggested city leaders consider whether the money could instead support community events, including Christmas tree lightings, concerts and food truck festivals, that could encourage residents to spend money within St. George.
The program will be funded through the City of St. George and the Uber Transit Innovation Fund. Funding is limited, and the city says the program could be modified as officials evaluate its performance.
The city may also offer additional ride subsidies during holidays, festivals and special events.
Enrollment information is expected to be released before the pilot launches later this year.
